editorial:
Imagine you are stuck in a quiet girls' school in the middle of the Civil War. Everything is calm and predictable until a wounded soldier from the opposing side shows up at the door. You get to watch these women, who have lived very sheltered lives, suddenly deal with a man who knows exactly how to charm them. The vibe is slow and heavy, making you feel the tension grow every time the soldier enters a room. It is less about big battles and more about the psychological games people play when they are trapped together in one house.

What really works here is the acting, as the women shift from being kind to being completely cold. The pacing is a bit slow, which might bore you if you want constant action, but the twist at the end makes the wait worth it. If you enjoy stories about power and secrets, you should definitely give this a try. It looks beautiful, so I suggest streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the detail, or you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: The movie ends in a dark way. The women realize the soldier is just manipulating them to survive. Instead of letting him go or killing him quickly, they decide to punish him together. They trick him and eventually kill him in a cold, calculated move. They then act like they are grieving and innocent, showing that the soldier actually turned the sheltered girls into cold killers themselves. They win, but they lose their innocence.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves slow-burn thrillers and psychological games.
